Load NFL schedules through nflreadr

Source: R/ingestion.R
load_nfl_schedule.Rd

Downloads schedule data with nflreadr::load_schedules() and caches the result in memory for the rest of the R session. The cached object is keyed by the requested seasons, so repeated calls with the same seasons do not re-download.

Usage

load_nfl_schedule(
  seasons = 2024:2025,
  refresh = FALSE,
  cache = getOption("nflrest.cache", TRUE),
  fix_neutral_venues = TRUE
)

Arguments

seasons

Integer vector of seasons to load. nflverse schedule data starts in 1999.

refresh

If TRUE, ignore any cached value and download again.

cache

If FALSE, bypass the cache for this call.

fix_neutral_venues

If TRUE (default), repair neutral-site games whose live stadium_id is missing or still points at the designated home team's own stadium. The bundled 2024-2025 sample supplies the actual venue for those games; seasons and venues outside the sample are left unchanged.

Value

A tibble of schedule data as returned by nflreadr::load_schedules(), including game_id, gameday, gametime, teams, scores, rest, spread, location, and stadium_id when available.

Details

Requires the suggested package nflreadr. The first call needs network access; later calls in the same session reuse the in-memory copy. Use clear_nflrest_cache() to release it. The returned columns are whatever nflreadr::load_schedules() provides, except that known 2024-2025 neutral-site venues can be repaired with fix_neutral_venues.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
schedule <- load_nfl_schedule(2024:2025)
clear_nflrest_cache()
} # }
